title: FDR Fireside Chats
identity_notes: Frozen GRH container preserves 31 numbered Franklin D. Roosevelt radio addresses corresponding to the FDR Presidential Library list of 31 speeches identified as Fireside Chats. Institutional audiovisual guidance explicitly says the category is disputed: 28 definite, two questionable, and potentially as many as 33 under an extended definition.

historical_context.title: Great Depression and New Deal public explanation
historical_context.description: The early identified chats address banking, recovery, employment, social security, agriculture, the judiciary and economic policy.

historical_context.title: Presidential radio communication and the Fireside Chat form
historical_context.description: Roosevelt used radio addresses framed as direct public communication; the institutional category itself has a disputed boundary.

historical_context.title: European war and American defense mobilization
historical_context.description: The middle identified chats shift toward war in Europe, defense, Lend-Lease, national emergency, freedom of the seas and U.S. entry into war.

historical_context.title: World War II home front and military progress
historical_context.description: The later identified chats cover war progress, sacrifice, price controls, labor, Italy, war loans, Allied conferences, economic rights and postwar plans.
